nodes.label: Body foundation for product specific content
nodes.rationale: Body supplies visual roles for on demand Cards, Widgets and other product content; products retain their own structure, data and rules instead of promoting each composition to a DS component.

nodes.label: Body component token alias chain
nodes.rationale: The 33 Body tokens belong to the existing component collection and resolve through semantic roles to existing primitives in four modes. Product content uses Body while official controls retain their own component tokens; resolved values and direct primitive consumption are excluded.

nodes.label: Five editable Body demonstration frames
nodes.rationale: The five Playground samples are editable frames with official DS control instances. They create no Card masters, sets, public exports, component family registration or component documentation.

nodes.label: Body warning strong contrast role
nodes.rationale: warning-strong aliases existing amber/800 because warning-default lacks normal text contrast on the two Body backgrounds. Strong brand roles support small text, and the warning meaning must also appear in text without altering existing component aliases.

nodes.label: Five Body typography styles
nodes.rationale: Shared bound Figma styles use Manrope and the existing derived weights, tracking and line heights: H1 24/32, H2 20/28, H3 16/24 semibold, description 14/20 and caption 12/16 regular. Visual size does not prescribe product HTML heading hierarchy.

nodes.label: Body gap and padding scale
nodes.rationale: Body spacing xl/lg/md/sm/xs/null resolves to 32/24/16/8/4/0 px via existing semantic aliases. Body size names do not rename the semantic scale; the same roles serve gaps and padding.

nodes.label: Body radius scale
nodes.rationale: Body radius lg/md/sm/null resolves to 16/8/4/0 px via radius-xl/md/sm/none, enabling product content to choose an existing Body radius.

nodes.label: Exterior separation between independent Cards and blocks
nodes.rationale: The user explicitly set exterior separation between independent Cards or information blocks to body/spacing/xl, 32 px. This spacing is distinct from all internal Card measurements.

nodes.label: Internal Card spacing standard
nodes.rationale: The initial internal composition uses 24 px padding, 16 px between segments, 8 px within segments and 4 px between title and description. Products may adjust with defined Body tokens; these values do not prescribe universal Card anatomy or a Card catalogue.

nodes.label: Body web exterior block spacing
nodes.rationale: The Body content column and demo rows consume body-spacing-xl for gaps, and content padding uses the same role. This implements the exterior 32 px layout while preserving a flexible content region.

nodes.label: Body web internal demo spacing
nodes.rationale: Local demo compositions consume body-spacing-lg for padding, md for segment gaps, sm within an information segment and xs between title and description. Background and radius also use Body aliases rather than resolved values.

nodes.label: Body web typography and text role consumption
nodes.rationale: Web headings, descriptions and captions consume Body family, weight, tracking, size and line-height aliases. Brand and status text consume their Body text color roles.

nodes.label: Body documentary acceptance and authorized scope
nodes.rationale: Documentary QA accepts the existing component to semantic to primitive architecture and distinct exterior 32 px versus interior 24/16/8/4 scales. It authorizes tokens, styles and five distinct demonstration frames in Figma and web; publication and installation were not requested.

nodes.label: Body token and contrast QA evidence
nodes.rationale: Implementation QA reports 33 component tokens and warning-strong backed by amber/800, four-mode identity-chain validation, five bound Manrope styles, 440 bindings and 23 overrides reviewed, and minimum text contrast 4.501742 across seven inks, two backgrounds and four modes.

nodes.label: Body five frame App Shell composition QA
nodes.rationale: The official App Shell instance 347:2597 in Playground 203:93 contains five distinct FRAME demos in a Fill Body Slot, without Card components or catalogue entries. QA separately checks exterior 32 px and internal 24/16/8/4 and preserves official tokens for Buttons, Ghost Icon Buttons, Badges, Linear Progress and Checkboxes.

nodes.label: Body browser and consumer skill QA
nodes.rationale: TypeScript, Next build and 12 Node tests passed. Chrome checked five compositions, spacing, themes, contrast, menu widths, keyboard controls and local feedback. Skills use a verified Body snapshot; Ruby/Psych validated frontmatter while external quick_validate remained unavailable without PyYAML, and no dependency was installed.

nodes.label: Registered Body foundation contract
nodes.rationale: The contract registry records FOUNDATIONS-BODY-001 with 33 tokens, five typography styles, internal 24/16/8/4 and exterior 32 px, explicitly retaining the samples as local frames rather than a Card family.

nodes.label: Registered Body Playground implementation
nodes.rationale: The implementation registry links official App Shell based Playground Body, its five frames with linked controls, Figma readback and delegated token data.

nodes.label: Registered Body Figma and Chrome QA
nodes.rationale: The QA registry records passing token, typography, contrast, measurement and demonstration checks in Figma and Chrome without adding consumable Card components.

nodes.label: Body user spacing and demonstration requirements
nodes.rationale: The source registry preserves the explicit user request for product specific Body roles, 32 px exterior Card separation, internal 24/16/8/4 and five different button or widget demos as App Shell frames outside component documentation.

nodes.label: Figma screen skill verified Body foundation lookup
nodes.rationale: For on demand product compositions, the skill opens the Body contract and JSON by verified snapshot paths instead of treating Body as a component family in the index. It requires alias lookup, Body typography and spacing, and preservation of official controls with their own tokens.

nodes.label: PO prototype skill verified Body foundation lookup
nodes.rationale: For on demand prototype content, the skill reads Body foundation and data by verified snapshot paths rather than a component index intent. Body size names must resolve through their aliases; embedded official controls preserve their own component tokens and demos do not define a Card family.
